{{irci|bancus|In most of Western continental Europe, floors are numbered as in Britain: the "first storey" or "first floor" is the next level above ground level. This system is used in Denmark but not in the other Scandinavian countries[2] This scheme is also used in many of the Commonwealth nations (except Singapore and most of Canada), many former British colonies, and in many (but not all) Latin American countries, including Mexico and Brazil.}}
